newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive saw pick-up in Q4 1996.
newsitem.headline: Incentive saw pick-up in Q4 1996.

text.p: Swedish investment group Incentive AB, whose main business area is medical technology, on Friday posted higher profits for 1996, saying fourth quarter sales and operating profit rose 18 percent.

Incentive reported its profit after financial items including associated companies rose to 5.23 billion crowns from 4.65 billion crowns in 1995. The market had expected a profit of 5.35 billion crowns.
Earnings in 1996 included non-recurring income of 2.57 billion crowns against 474 million crowns a year earlier.
"The year closed with a quarter that was stronger than the year-earlier period in terms of revenues and earnings...both increased by 18 percent," Incentive said in a statement.
"The trend of revenues in the European market was still weak but the trend in North America and Asia continued to be favourable."
Incentive posted 1996 sales of 20.22 billion crowns with sales of companies increasing by 17 percent against 1995 when sales reach 24.32 billion.
It said 150 million crowns was wiped off earnings in the present group structure by foreign exchange movements.
Incentive said a reorganisation of the group in 1996 had resulted in fewer business areas with well positioned operations.
"At the same time its financial position has been strengthened significantly," the company said.
It had bought the outstanding shares of the Gambro medical technology company, whose sales amounted to 10.96 billion crowns in 1996 against 10.16 billion in 1995.
Operations that accounted for nearly a third of the group's revenues were divested including Hasselblad, Garphyttan and Skandinaviska Elverk (SEV).
The sale of SEV reduced net debt by nearly six billion crowns.
"Following the sale of the trading and power organisations, it is strongly internationalised, with more than 90 percent of sales outside Sweden," Incentive said.
Group investments during the year amounted to 1.26 billion crowns compared to 1.55 billion crowns in 1995.
Following two transactions this year, Incentive said net debt would be reduced by about two billion crowns to 8.3 billion crowns.

These were the sale of 2.8 billion Electrolux shares worth 1.2 billion crowns with an estimated capital gain of 360 million crowns and a preliminary agreement to sell a holding in U.S. group Wabco worth about 810 million crowns for a capital gain of about 65 million crowns.
Incentive proposed a 1996 dividend of 10 crowns, a rise of one crown from 1995.
